Why exactly is it that cake artist are so undervalued? Why do people haggle and try to get a bargain basement price? Baking, assembling and decorating a cake is no different or less time-consuming than making any other hand crafted item that people are more than willing to spend money on. The only difference is, it doesn't last as long.

The most common answer to that from people …

“It’s ONLY cake”

I personally think (feel free to give your input) images are conjured up like what are seen on all of these cake wars shows. They have 1 hour to bake, stack, decorate beautiful cakes. People see this and think, “well it isn’t that hard, doesn’t take very long” etc. Meanwhile behind the scenes extra cakes are already baked, batches – yes batches of buttercream are already made – there are hours between filming, decorating that you don’t see. Most people have no idea and I don’t hold that against them at all, more people need to be educated about what goes into “just a cake”. “Well anyone can make a cake, it isn’t hard” – if that were the case, grocery store bakeries, small run bakeries and home based bakers wouldn’t exist! While “anyone can make a cake” just like “anyone can take a great photo” – it does not make them a photographer!

While I applaud anyone willing to put the time and effort into making their own cake for a celebration, more often than not it doesn’t turn out as planned unless they truly have a natural gift for baking. For me the main thing is you gave it a go at seeing if you could do it.

I sat down this morning while having my coffee and worked out that I have spent almost $3000 – yes you read that right, on CLASSES to help me become a better cake artist. While I am not perfect at everything (i'll be the first to admit it), I have made sure to master the basics.

I've taken classes ranging from buttercream techniques, wafer paper, party cakes, sculpted cakes, handbag cakes, the list goes on!! I haven’t even calculated the cost of all my cake decorating tools etc that I have (I think not only would my husband have a heart attack but I would too at the final total). I would love nothing more to win the lottery so I could attend in person classes with some of my favorite cake artists – which by the way cost hundreds of dollars – sometimes $400 for a 12 hour class. At this point in time I can’t afford that and none of them are local so I would have to travel hours (yet another cost). Side note: I may have a slight obsession with cake stands! There are actually a few not in the picture hahaha.

I have invested money as you can see and many, many hours of time to be able to produce a wonderful looking product. So to me and many others, it is not “just a cake”. It is a piece of our heart, soul and mind that goes into every cake. It is insulting and it is hurtful to hear “just a cake”.

With doing a custom cake, comes many hours, sore feet, sore backs and working until 3am in the morning & time away from being with our families. Most people are totally unaware of this though and I do try educate them without being rude or condescending about it. I will use an example below and break it down, not picked for any particular reason other than to break down the hours that went into it.

The example below was a cake that I was more than happy to donate to a very special little person!! Despite the long hours that went into it, I had a blast and it was worth it to see the look on a little face!

Frozen Cake that was donated

Baking the layers fresh – 3 hours
Making buttercream (real buttercream) – 1 hour
Making my own fondant & coloring it – 2 hours
Torting (cutting layers, filling with buttercream) – 1 hour
Buttercream finish – 1 hour
Decorations, trees, edible “glass”, snowflakes (includes drying time) – 2 hours
Covering with fondant – 1 hour
Making and applying ruffles – 1 1/2 hours
Making the fondant board & drying time – 3 hours
Cutting letters & drying time – 2 hours
TOTAL TIME = 17 1/2 HOURS! – I totally left out making modeling chocolate from scratch 
or the edible glass!! So add more time!

You think when you go to work for 17 1/2 hours what you get paid – lets say you work that 17 1/2 hours at $10 an hour, before taxes etc you would make $175. That is just for your HOURS, now imagine you had to purchase all the ingredients needed too.

Powdered sugar
Eggs
Milk
Flour
Sugar
Flavorings
Baking powder/soda
Marshmallows (to make fondant)
Butter
Chocolate (for modeling chocolate)

Now imagine your boss comes over and says to you – “Well you did great work for those 17 1/2 hours, however I am only willing to pay your for 3 maybe 4 hours”. There would be outrage if that happened. Cake artists face this on a daily basis though. DAILY!

I am lucky enough I have had the funds to be able to learn all of the things that I know and I can make cakes for family celebrations, so I don’t have to go to anyone else to get my cakes, cookies, cupcakes or cake pops. Which is why I started this whole adventure - I couldn't afford the price tags that came along with the type of cakes I wanted at celebrations.

I would love a new car with all the custom features or a really nice designer handbag but I can’t afford them. Custom anything isn’t cheap, you can’t get a Ferrari on a GMC budget.

Please keep in mind the next time you order a custom cake, exactly what goes into it and if you value the artist (whoever it is) to pay them what they ask (which includes their time). You can always change designs and elements to change the price, which I am more than happy to work with, I want someone that contacts me to have something as close to what they wanted, rather than be put right off of trying to order something that is custom.

I have a recent client that happens to hate the artificial aspect of grocery cakes and knows the value of what goes into a custom cake, including the price. They have been a breath of fresh air as I haven’t had to explain any of the above to them, they already knew.

“Good cake isn’t cheap and cheap cake isn’t good”.
